stories.title: Study finds Grok API leans Republican, OpenAI API leans Democrat in forced vote question
stories.summary: A Convovo study asked the developer APIs of SpaceXAI’s Grok 4.7 and OpenAI’s GPT‑6.1 Sol to name a single candidate for upcoming midterm races without hedging. Grok recommended the Republican in 92 % of responses, while GPT‑6.1 Sol chose the Democrat in 97 %, and the models agreed on less than 10 % of nearly 500 races. The consumer chatbots for both services refused to answer, and OpenAI said the API test does not reflect typical user experience.
stories.why: The findings suggest that political bias in developer‑facing AI models could influence public opinion when integrated into third‑party applications.
stories.previousTitle: Forced to pick, Grok’s AI model chooses Republicans. OpenAI’s picks Democrats.
stories.previousSummary: A new study found that when forced to choose in this year’s upcoming midterm elections, SpaceXAI’s Grok 4.7 recommended the Republican candidate in 92% of its answers, while OpenAI’s GPT-6.1 Sol picked the Democrat in 97%. Across nearly 500 races, the two models agreed less than 10% of the time.

stories.title: Three arrested in Waterford arson investigation released without charge
stories.summary: Gardaí have released three people who were arrested in connection with the suspected arson that destroyed a home on Birch Avenue in Waterford, killing Philip and Kim English and their children Jayden, 9, and Callum, 12. The arrests were made earlier this month, and a man in his 20s and a woman in her 30s have already been charged in relation to the attack. No further arrests have been reported.
stories.why: It illustrates the progress and challenges of the police investigation and legal handling of a high‑profile homicide case.

stories.summary: German companies are increasingly viewing India as a strategic manufacturing and innovation hub for the future. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said German companies are increasingly viewing India as a hub for manufacturing, research and development, and innovation, beyond its traditional role as a consumer market.

stories.title: India and Russia aim for $100 billion trade by 2030
stories.summary: Indian Ambassador Vinay Kumar said India and Russia will work to raise bilateral trade to about $100 billion by 2030. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Vladimir Putin have directed efforts to boost mutual investments, and the plan was discussed at the BRICS summit in New Delhi. India also pledged to train qualified workers for Russian industry needs.
stories.why: The increase would deepen economic ties and diversify supply chains for both countries.
